name: r2-across-1
statement: The RL-Zero-Math weight change acts, to first order, as a logit shift that collapses next-token entropy only at the base's own high-entropy fork positions and leaves low-entropy positions alone, so the RL model carries a fork-local low temperature: global temperature barely moves RL because its forks are already near one-hot, whereas for the base, cooling to T 0.6 also sharpens the easy restatement step at diffuse forks and starts loops, and heating to T 1.0 removes loops but samples wrong branches at the forks; any partial delta (attention-only, MLP-only, a times the delta) collapses fork entropy partly and stays temperature-sensitive in proportion to the fork entropy it leaves.
scope: Olmo-3-1025-7B base (plain and cued) vs Olmo-3.1-7B-RL-Zero-Math and partial copies of its delta (n13 arms, base + a*(RL - base)), MATH-500 and the 328, T 0.6-1.4, top-p 0.95-1.0, cap 16,384, grader v3. Covers the temperature dependence of accuracy, cap hits and loops, and the per-position entropy/KL readouts. Does not cover the 'Answer:' format switch (a change at a low-entropy position), Olmo-3.0 RL, the Code pair, or pass@k.

imports.finding: RL without entropy control collapses policy entropy early (most of it in the first ~200 steps) and accuracy follows R = -a exp(H) + b; a low-entropy policy is insensitive to sampling temperature.
imports.how: Explains why Olmo-3.1 RL moves -0.2 points between T 0.6 and T 1.0 while the cued base moves +6.4, and predicts RL holds near 92 % even at T 1.3, and that RL's per-token entropy on its own answers is less than half the cued base's.

imports.finding: RLVR keeps the base's high-entropy minority positions (top 20 % by entropy) and changes entropy mainly there; training on the low-entropy 80 % does nothing.
imports.how: Localises the RL change in the team's disagreement map: predicts the top-20 % base-entropy positions hold most of KL(RL||base), which fits the top 4 % holding only 38.7 % and the 8 % top-1 disagreement rate, and makes the delta a fork-local cooling rather than a global one.

imports.finding: Loops arise at low temperature where the progress-making action's mass is diffused over alternatives while an easy cyclic action keeps its mass (risk aversion); temperature removes loops but not the underlying error.
imports.how: Explains why global cooling cannot reproduce RL: it sharpens the base's cyclic action at diffuse forks (98-119 cap hits at T 0.6), while RL's fork-local cooling puts the mass on the progress action, so a partial delta that leaves forks diffuse keeps extra cap hits at T 0.6 that vanish at T 1.0.

explains.how: RL's forks are near one-hot after entropy collapse, so dividing logits by 0.6 or 1.0 changes few sampled branches.
Global cooling of the base sharpens the cyclic restatement at diffuse forks, so loops appear at T 0.6 even without top-p.
Top-p 0.95 cools the tail further and adds loops, as expected when loops are set by how sharp the base's fork distributions become.
At T 1.0 the cyclic action no longer wins, loops vanish, and the remaining gap is wrong branches sampled at the base's still-diffuse forks.
Without the cue the plain base has even more diffuse forks, so heating costs ~28 points on short problems (wrong branches) and only breaks even on the longest ones where loops dominated.

explains.quote: cuts limit loops 59 -> 53, T 1 cuts to 24
explains.how: The same ordering (top-p removal helps a little, T 1 a lot) appears in an unrelated model, as a temperature-controlled loop onset predicts.
Even from RL's sound prefix the base still loops 21 times at T 0.6: the loop comes from the base's own fork distributions under cooling, not only from its prefix.

explains.quote: the +3.4 difference lies entirely in cap-hit problems
explains.how: Attention-only and MLP-only arms each collapse fork entropy partly; at T 0.6 the less complete arm keeps more diffuse forks and so more loop cap hits.

explains.quote: summed first-order scores predict a 0.542-nat drop
explains.how: The delta acts as a first-order logit shift, so a partial or scaled delta gives a proportionally partial fork cooling.

explains.quote: Top-1 tokens differ at 7.98 % of 1,966,404 T1 positions
explains.how: RL changes the argmax at a minority of positions, the size of the base's high-entropy fork set, and leaves the rest.

explains.quote: the top 4 % of positions carry 38.7 % of KL
explains.how: KL is spread over the ~20 % high-entropy fork positions, not concentrated in 1-4 %, as fork-local entropy change predicts.

conflicts.how: The largest log-ratio sits on an answer-format token where the base is likely confident, a change at a low-entropy position the theory does not cover.

conflicts.quote: At the base's true ends RL's P(stop) is below 0.5
conflicts.how: At stop positions RL makes the base's confident stop less certain, i.e. raises entropy there, the opposite direction to fork cooling.

conflicts.quote: Median tokens of right answers: base 1,432, RL 3,014
conflicts.how: RL writes longer answers; entropy collapse alone does not predict longer answers, so length needs the stop change above.
Misreads and slips are covered only if the decisive tokens of those errors sit at high-entropy forks, which is not measured.

rival: RL's temperature robustness and the base's loss come from a learned stop/budget controller (r1-across-2) or from suppressed self-copying in layers 0-15 (r1-across-1), with mid-solution fork entropy unchanged. Separation: (1) mean per-token entropy of RL on its own answers vs the cued base on its own: the rivals predict similar entropy away from stop tokens, this theory predicts RL below half the base's; (2) the n13 attention-only arm at T 1.0: this theory predicts its extra cap hits over MLP-only vanish, the self-copy rival predicts they persist because the copy pathway is still intact.

predictions.experiment: Olmo-3.1-7B-RL-Zero-Math, plain prompt, T 1.3 / top-p 1.0, MATH-500 n=500, one sample, cap 16,384, grader v3: right
predictions.refuted_by: fewer than 430 right (RL degrades with heating like a high-entropy policy)

predictions.experiment: Mean per-token entropy (nats, full-vocabulary distribution at T 1) of RL on its own 500 T 1.0 MATH-500 answers divided by that of the cued base on its own 500 T 1.0 answers, positions after the cue
On the fdc8da T1 texts (cued base answers), share of total KL(RL||base) mass located at the positions in the base's top 20 % by next-token entropy
n13 arm 'base + attention and norm delta only' (MLP stays base), plain prompt, T 1.0 / top-p 1.0, MATH-500 n=500, cap 16,384, grader v3: cap hits (and right)
predictions.refuted_by: 35 or more cap hits (the arm's cap-hit excess persists when loops are removed by temperature); expected right 430 [415, 445]

predictions.experiment: base + 0.5*(RL - base) on all tensors, opening cue, T 0.6 / top-p 1.0, MATH-500 n=500, cap 16,384, grader v3: cap hits (and right)
predictions.refuted_by: 70 or more cap hits (half the delta leaves the base's loop rate near its 98); expected right 440 [425, 455]
